items.reason: Pinning a tag to a commit SHA means asking GitHub what the tag points at right now, and this session has no network; scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update already does the whole close (rewrite + STRICT=true + ratchet) in one networked run, and inventing a SHA would break the workflow rather than pin it.

The read/write split the item asks for already existed (issue-dispatch.yml is three jobs: the one with the model key, the one that writes a ref, the one that can speak — none can do another's damage), and `contents: write` cannot be narrowed further because pushing a ref needs it; what was missing was that nothing bounded any grant, so rule P10 in scripts/actions-pin.mjs now compares every workflow's and job's permissions against .github/workflow-permissions.json in both directions and refuses a write with no recorded reason.

The rule does reach the path (A5 runs over the pushed range in agent-review.yml and over origin/master..HEAD in the pre-push hook) — it was drawn too narrow: `chore: partial work from an interrupted lane session` passed every existing narration rule and is in this log twice, so loop-mechanics now names lane/loop/harness/autopilot sessions and a new run-progress rule refuses a completeness word bound to a work noun.

The read-first set is now declared and measured — seven documents, 1538 lines, a ceiling on each and on the total — with everything else declared a lookup routed to by docs/task-index.md, and test-unit/guidance-budget.test.mjs blocking on every build.

Already covered another way and better than the item assumes: test-llm/adversarial/corpus.json places hostile payloads in the real product prompt builders (campaign names from an advertiser's console, public Google reviews, inbound messages), test-unit/llm-adversarial.test.mjs asserts detection, containment and refusal on every build, and scripts/injection-drill.mjs does the same for the harness's own model surfaces with a weekly live run.

Already covered: .github/contract-ledger.json carries a `ceiling` for every eslint fence exception list (adamant/seams 3, seams-lib 3, chokepoint 1, route-segment-config 0) and every SAST allowlist, and scripts/contract-ledger.mjs --check (blocking inside check:ci) fails when a list grows past it OR when an exception list carries no ceiling at all.

`npm run test:fast` runs the suites that name the files you changed plus the always tier in .github/test-tiers.json, under the same node flags as the gate, reporting a changed file no test claims; it is deliberately outside check:ci and test-unit/test-tier-census.test.mjs blocks if the tier rots or if somebody wires the subset in as a gate.

A health-gated staged rollout is Vercel-side configuration plus a promotion workflow that has to observe live signals; this session has no network, no platform access and no way to verify an abort path, and a rollout config that has never aborted anything is exactly the artefact the brief says not to substitute.

All twelve ADRs now carry a `## Revisit when` section naming falsifiable triggers (an observation, an event or a number — never a date), and scripts/adr-check.mjs rule 7 requires it on every record from the day it lands, blocking inside check:ci.

lessons: In this repository a new fence is never one file: a rule needs a row in .github/contract-ledger.json (with a ceiling or a floor if it measures anything), a row in .github/constraint-map.json AND the matching row in AGENTS.md's table in the same order, an entry in scripts/gate-remedy.mjs if it joins check:ci, and a test-unit file that points the real gate at a fixture and requires a red. test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs and scripts/contract-ledger.mjs enforce all of it, so a half-landed fence is a red build rather than a quiet one.

Prefer blocking through a test-unit file over adding a stage to check:ci. A new stage drags in gate-remedy entries, the constraint-map's every-stage-has-a-rule assertion and the cheapest-first timing baseline in .github/gate-timings.json; a unit test blocks through the same check:ci and pre-push path with none of that coupling — which is how env-manifest, perf-budget and the model pins are already wired.

Scan findings about this repository's governance are often already closed, because the fence exists one layer deeper than a scanner looks: exception-list ratchets live in the contract ledger rather than next to the eslint rule, and the adversarial eval corpus lives in test-llm/adversarial rather than in test-llm/golden. Read the ledger and the constraint map before building anything a finding asks for.

The commit subjects an automation lane writes are the repository's most reliably broken rule, and the cause is structural: the lane takes the first line of the agent's report and uses it as the subject, in a worktree where no hook is installed. The fix that works is to write the report's first line AS a conventional-commit subject, and to keep extending scripts/commit-subject.mjs from the log rather than from imagination.
